title: Child Safe Standards and Reportable Conduct guidance moving to the SSR website
body: From 1 October 2026, guidance and resources on the Child Safe Standards and Reportable Conduct Scheme will move from the Commission for Children and Young People website to the Social Services Regulator website. Legal obligations will not change, but clubs should review links to Commission information in their websites, policies and other materials and update them where required. Clubs should continue to contact the SSR about both schemes.
verifiedQuote: From 1 October 2026, information, including guidance and resources, about the Child Safe Standards and Reportable Conduct Scheme will move from the Commission for Children and Young People website to the Social Services Regulator (SSR) website.
correction: The draft states guidance 'moved' (past tense) but the source clearly states it 'will move' (future tense) from 1 October 2026, and the draft incorrectly says 'keep contacting' when the source says 'continue to contact'.

title: Unfinished WWC Check applications may be deleted from 19 October
body: Anyone who starts an online Working with Children Check application but doesn't complete it, including verifying their identity, before Monday 19 October 2026 may have their application deleted. They will then need to start a new application and complete the mandatory child safety training.
verifiedQuote: If you start an online application but don't complete it before Monday 19 October 2026, including verifying your identity, your application may be deleted. You will then need to start a new application and complete the mandatory child safety training.
correction: The draft incorrectly stated applications 'may be deleted' and incorrectly referred to 'coaches and volunteers' and 'clubs' when the source doesn't mention sport specifically, but the core claim about incomplete applications is supported.

title: WWC Connect: seven-year record keeping and setup guidance for organisations
body: From 19 October 2026, organisations that engage people in child-related work must keep records of each worker's name, contact details, evidence of verification, and start and end dates for at least seven years after they stop engaging them. Clubs access WWC Connect with a Service Victoria account and business profile, and can add delegates and use bulk upload.
verifiedQuote: You must keep these records for at least seven years after you stop engaging the person in child-related work.
correction: The draft incorrectly states records must be kept for seven years 'after they stop, or commit an offence'—the source only mentions after they stop working; also overstates what guidance 'confirms' about unincorporated associations.

title: WA: Interstate Working with Children Check bans now recognised in WA
body: Changes to WA's Working with Children Check laws are now in effect, so if a person receives an adverse WWC Check decision in another Australian state or territory, that decision is also recognised in WA. There is no transition period, and all pending applicants and card holders are covered from 17 September 2026. If an organisation becomes aware that an employee, volunteer or student is subject to an adverse interstate WWC decision, they must immediately take steps to ensure the person does not continue engaging in child-related work, including those accessing the child or parent volunteer exemption.
verifiedQuote: Under these changes, if a person receives an adverse WWC Check decision in another Australian state or territory, that decision will also be recognised in WA. Put simply: banned in one, banned in all.
correction: The source supports the core facts but states the 'Working with Children (Screening) Act 2024' not 2004, uses 'adverse interstate WWC decision' not 'adverse WWC Check decision', and mentions the volunteer declaration has been updated but doesn't claim a template was updated or specify information sessions are free.
